description: We are Svetla and Anelia, final-year Biomedical Engineering students at the Medical University of Varna. Passionate about science, technology, and innovation, we are excited to participate in the 2026 NASA Hackathon. We hope to bring our biomedical knowledge, creativity, and problem-solving skills to the team, explore innovative solutions to real-world challenges, and gain valuable experience while contributing fresh perspectives.
summary: Orbital Eye AI is a web application that helps astronauts and flight surgeons monitor eye health during long-duration missions, focusing on Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS) - one of NASA's top health risks for long missions. Crew members upload retinal OCT scans taken before, during and after flight. The app checks image quality, detects retinal layer boundaries, measures retinal thickness and compares every new scan against that astronaut's own pre-flight baseline. When the change exceeds a set threshold, it raises a "recommend ophthalmological review" alert. On Moon and Mars missions, real time help from ground experts will not be possible, so crews need onboard tools that turn OCT images into actionable trends. This is a research prototype and does not diagnose SANS
details:
ORBITAL EYE AI is an AI-powered medical monitoring concept designed to help protect astronauts' vision during long-duration space missions. Our project focuses on Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS), a condition associated with spaceflight that can cause changes in the eye and visual system.

The proposed system uses Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) imaging and artificial intelligence to analyze retinal structures, identify potential changes, and monitor their progression over time. By establishing individual baseline measurements and comparing subsequent scans, ORBITAL EYE AI aims to support early detection of vision-related abnormalities and provide valuable information for medical teams.

We developed a web-based prototype using Python, Flask, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and SQLite. It includes an astronaut monitoring dashboard, patient profiles, OCT image upload functionality, and a framework for integrating AI-based image analysis using deep learning techniques such as U-Net segmentation.

Our project combines biomedical engineering, medical imaging, and artificial intelligence to address a real challenge in human space exploration. We considered astronaut safety, data accuracy, limited medical resources, remote monitoring, and the need for reliable healthcare solutions during missions to the Moon and Mars.

Our intended impact is to support safer long-duration space missions by providing a foundation for intelligent, personalized vision monitoring. In the future, the technology could also be adapted for remote ophthalmology and retinal health monitoring on Earth.

As biomedical engineering students, we approached this challenge by combining our medical knowledge with software development to explore how AI can help protect human health beyond Earth.
